# Purpose

This notebook builds the Danaini (butterfly) species tree from the sequence data retrieved in
**Step 1** (`1_pull_ncbi_data.Rmd`). It reads only from `input_data/` — no network access — and
produces the **multi-locus supermatrix tree**: every Danaini species with **at least one** of the 12
loci, plus three outgroup species, concatenated into a partitioned supermatrix and inferred by
maximum likelihood.

The full approach:

1. select species from the occupancy matrix (≥1 locus, plus outgroups);
2. **codon-aware alignment** of each locus (best reading frame → translate → MAFFT on amino acids →
   back-translate);
3. **automated QC/trim** of each alignment (dense codon-column core; drop sequences with excess
   gaps, internal stops, or consensus-outlier distances; one sequence per species);
4. **concatenate** into a supermatrix with **codon-position partitions**;
5. infer the ML tree with **IQ-TREE** (run as a documented manual step — see §6);
6. **root** on *Heliconius erato*, then export the tree and its branch-support values.

All QC is automated and every dropped sequence and the reason for it is logged to `output_data/curation/`.

# 0. Setup

## 0.1 Libraries and helpers

The functions below are sourced from the shared `helpers/` folder.

```{r libs}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(tidyverse)
  library(Biostrings)
  library(ape)
  library(ggtree)
})

# Helpers are sourced by RELATIVE path: the working directory must be the code/
# folder. Chunk-by-chunk in VS Code uses the workspace root as wd, not the .Rmd
# folder — so check and fail loudly if it's wrong.
if (!file.exists("helpers/sequence_utils.R")) {
  stop("Can't find helpers/ — set the working directory to code/ first.\n",
       "  Current getwd(): ", getwd(), "\n",
       '  Run: setwd("<path>/Extended_Data_Figure1/code")  (or restart the R terminal there)')
}
source("helpers/sequence_utils.R")    # get_accession, standardize_taxon, ...
source("helpers/codon_alignment.R")   # codon_align()  (Marianna, refactored by Naama)
source("helpers/alignment_qc.R")      # auto_trim_and_qc(), process_locus()  (Naama)
source("helpers/supermatrix_tree.R")  # concat_loci, partitions, root_and_plot, export_tree
```

## 0.2 Configuration

```{r config}
# Paths are relative to the code/ folder (the working directory). Reads come from
# input_data/danaini_tree/; generated artifacts go to output_data/danaini_tree/,
# figures to visuals/danaini_tree/.
INPUT_ROOT <- Sys.getenv("DANAINI_INPUT", unset = "../input_data/danaini_tree")
OUT_ROOT   <- Sys.getenv("DANAINI_OUT",   unset = "../output_data/danaini_tree")
FIG_ROOT   <- Sys.getenv("DANAINI_FIG",   unset = "../visuals/danaini_tree")

INGROUP_DIR  <- file.path(INPUT_ROOT, "ncbi_loci")        # read: Danaini sequences
OUTGROUP_DIR <- file.path(INPUT_ROOT, "ncbi_outgroups")   # read: outgroup sequences
CURATION_DIR <- file.path(OUT_ROOT, "curation")           # write: per-locus QC logs
TREE_DIR     <- file.path(OUT_ROOT, "supermatrix_ge1")    # write: supermatrix + tree
for (d in c(CURATION_DIR, TREE_DIR, FIG_ROOT)) dir.create(d, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# External tools — installed in a dedicated conda env (project preference; not Homebrew).
CONDA_BIN <- "/opt/anaconda3/envs/danaini-phylo/bin"
pick_bin <- function(cands) {
  for (b in cands) {
    p <- file.path(CONDA_BIN, b); if (file.exists(p)) return(p)
    w <- Sys.which(b);            if (nzchar(w)) return(unname(w))
  }
  ""
}
MAFFT_BIN  <- pick_bin("mafft")                       # needed by this notebook (alignment)
IQTREE_BIN <- pick_bin(c("iqtree3", "iqtree2", "iqtree"))  # referenced only by the manual §6 step
stopifnot(nzchar(MAFFT_BIN))
message("MAFFT : ", MAFFT_BIN)
message("IQTREE: ", if (nzchar(IQTREE_BIN)) IQTREE_BIN else "(not found — run §6 manually)")

# Loci, genetic codes, outgroups, thresholds.
LOCI  <- c("COI","ArgKin","CAD","DDC","EF1a","GAPDH","IDH","MDH","RpS5","RpS2","wg","Atpa")
CODE5 <- Biostrings::getGeneticCode("5")             # invertebrate mitochondrial (COI)
GCODE_OF <- function(locus) if (locus == "COI") CODE5 else Biostrings::GENETIC_CODE

OUTGROUPS_RAW <- c("Tellervo zoilus", "Mechanitis polymnia", "Heliconius erato")
OUTGROUPS_STD <- gsub(" ", "_", OUTGROUPS_RAW)
ROOT_TAXON    <- "Heliconius_erato"                  # most distant outgroup species

OCC_THRESHOLD <- 0.5     # min codon-column occupancy to keep in the trim core
MAX_BAD       <- 0.20    # max gap/ambiguity fraction per sequence
MAD_K         <- 4       # consensus-distance outlier cutoff (median + k*MAD)
MIN_LOCI      <- 1L      # multi-locus tree: keep species with >= 1 locus (supermatrix_ge1)
SEED          <- 12345
```

# 1. Species selection

Read the occupancy matrix from `input_data/` and keep ingroup species with at least `MIN_LOCI` loci,
plus the three outgroup species (needed for rooting).

```{r select-species}
occ <- read_csv(file.path(INPUT_ROOT, "occupancy_matrix.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
keep_raw <- occ %>%
  filter(n_loci >= MIN_LOCI | butterfly_species %in% OUTGROUPS_RAW) %>%
  pull(butterfly_species)
keep_std <- union(gsub(" ", "_", keep_raw), OUTGROUPS_STD)
cat("Species requested (>=", MIN_LOCI, "locus/loci + outgroups):", length(keep_std), "\n")
```

# 2. Per-locus codon alignment + automated QC

The chunk below runs the entire align → QC → select chain for every locus: each
`process_locus()` call (in `helpers/alignment_qc.R`, delegating to `auto_trim_and_qc()`) returns a
single sequence per species for that locus. Because Step 1 kept up to 3 candidate accessions per
species×locus, this is also where **the one accession that will represent each species is chosen**.
For each locus:

1. **Gather candidates** — `read_combined_locus()` loads all retrieved ingroup + outgroup
   sequences; a species may enter with several candidate accessions.
2. **Align them jointly** — `codon_align()` codon-aligns every candidate together (best reading
   frame → translate → MAFFT on amino acids → back-translate). Nothing is dropped yet.
3. **Trim to the dense core** — keep only codon columns present in ≥ `OCC_THRESHOLD` (0.5) of
   sequences, which strips sparse insertions and mRNA-only tails while preserving reading frame.
4. **Flag bad sequences** — a candidate is dropped if its gap/ambiguity fraction over the core
   exceeds `MAX_BAD` (0.20), it has more than one internal stop codon, or it is a consensus
   distance-outlier (> median + `MAD_K`·MAD, `MAD_K` = 4). **Outgroup species are protected** and
   never dropped (legitimately divergent, and needed to root the tree).
5. **Choose one accession per species** — among a species' surviving candidates, pick the one with
   the **lowest gap fraction** over the trimmed core, breaking ties by **most non-gap bases**
   (longest). That accession is marked `selected = TRUE` and becomes the species' row in the
   alignment (and later its entry in `chosen_accessions.csv` / the reference matrix).

Every candidate and the reason it was kept or dropped is recorded per locus in
`output_data/curation/<locus>_qc_log.csv`, so the choices are fully auditable.

```{r align-qc}
aln_list <- setNames(lapply(LOCI, function(lc) process_locus(lc, keep_std = keep_std)), LOCI)
```

# 3. Concatenate into a partitioned supermatrix

```{r concat}
cc <- concat_loci(aln_list)
writeXStringSet(cc$super, file.path(TREE_DIR, "supermatrix.fasta"))
write_csv(cc$partitions, file.path(TREE_DIR, "partitions.csv"))
write_codon_partitions(cc$partitions, file.path(TREE_DIR, "partitions_codon.nex"))
cat("Supermatrix:", length(cc$super), "species x", unique(width(cc$super)), "bp\n")
```

# 4. Record the chosen accessions

The single accession chosen per species×locus (the sequences that actually entered the supermatrix),
aggregated from the per-locus QC logs just written. This is saved two ways: a tidy long table
(`chosen_accessions.csv`) and the **species×gene reference matrix** (`accession_reference_matrix.csv`)
— a wide, non-tidy table with **species on the rows (y)** and **genes on the columns (x)**, each cell
holding the one chosen accession (blank where the species contributed no sequence for that gene).

```{r chosen}
chosen <- map_dfr(LOCI, function(lc) {
  f <- file.path(CURATION_DIR, paste0(lc, "_qc_log.csv"))
  if (!file.exists(f)) return(NULL)
  read_csv(f, show_col_types = FALSE) %>% filter(selected) %>%
    transmute(species, locus, accession)
}) %>% filter(species %in% names(cc$super)) %>% arrange(species, locus)

write_csv(chosen, file.path(TREE_DIR, "chosen_accessions.csv"))
cat("Wrote chosen_accessions.csv:", nrow(chosen), "species x locus sequences\n")

# Reference matrix: species (rows) x genes (columns), cells = the chosen accession.
accession_matrix <- chosen %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = locus, values_from = accession) %>%
  select(species, any_of(LOCI)) %>%          # genes on the x axis, in canonical order
  arrange(species)
write_csv(accession_matrix, file.path(OUT_ROOT, "accession_reference_matrix.csv"))
cat("Reference matrix:", nrow(accession_matrix), "species x",
    ncol(accession_matrix) - 1, "genes\n")
```

# 5. Build the ML tree with IQ-TREE (run manually)

The maximum-likelihood search is **not run from R** — it is the one heavy, long-running step, so we
keep it explicit and reproducible as a shell command you run yourself in the conda env. The chunk
below is **not evaluated** (`eval=FALSE`); copy it into a terminal.

```{bash iqtree, eval=FALSE}
# Activate the dedicated conda env that holds IQ-TREE 3 (and MAFFT).
conda activate danaini-phylo        # or: /opt/anaconda3/envs/danaini-phylo/bin on PATH

# From the code/ folder; the supermatrix lives under the shared output_data/ tree.
cd ../output_data/danaini_tree/supermatrix_ge1

# ML tree with ModelFinderPlus + partition merging, 1000 ultrafast-bootstrap replicates
# (--bnni reduces UFBoot overestimation). -p applies the codon-position partition scheme.
iqtree3 \
  -s supermatrix.fasta \
  -p partitions_codon.nex \
  -m MFP+MERGE \
  -B 1000 --bnni \
  -T AUTO \
  -seed 12345 \
  -pre supermatrix_ge1 \
  -redo

# Key outputs written next to the inputs:
#   supermatrix_ge1.treefile   ML tree, internal-node labels = UFBoot support
#   supermatrix_ge1.contree    majority-rule consensus tree
#   supermatrix_ge1.iqtree     full report (models, partitions, likelihoods)
#   supermatrix_ge1.log        run log
```

# 6. Root, export, and plot the tree

Run this **after** IQ-TREE has produced `supermatrix_ge1.treefile`. The chunk is guarded by
`file.exists()`, so the notebook still knits cleanly before the tree has been built. It roots on
*Heliconius erato* and writes three things: the rooted tree in newick, a table of branch-support
values, and a figure with the support values drawn at the internal nodes.

```{r root-export-plot}
treefile    <- file.path(TREE_DIR, "supermatrix_ge1.treefile")
out_newick  <- file.path(TREE_DIR, "supermatrix_ge1_rooted.newick")
out_support <- file.path(TREE_DIR, "branch_support.csv")
out_pdf     <- file.path(FIG_ROOT, "supermatrix_ge1_tree.pdf")

if (file.exists(treefile)) {
  rt <- root_and_plot(treefile, out_pdf,
                      title = "Danaini — ≥1-locus supermatrix (ML, UFBoot support)")
  sup <- export_tree(rt, out_newick, out_support)
  cat("Rooted tree tips:", length(rt$tip.label), "\n")
  cat("Wrote:", out_newick, "|", out_support, "|", out_pdf, "\n")
  cat("Branch-support summary:\n"); print(summary(sup$support))
} else {
  message("No treefile yet at ", treefile,
          " — run the IQ-TREE command in §5, then re-knit to root/export/plot.")
}
```

# Notes

- **QC thresholds** (`OCC_THRESHOLD`, `MAX_BAD`, `MAD_K`) are the automated-QC knobs; the per-locus
  `output_data/curation/*_qc_log.csv` files record every dropped sequence and why, so the thresholds
  can be tuned if the logs show over- or under-aggressive filtering.
- **Outgroups are protected** from the consensus-outlier filter (they are legitimately divergent);
  if an outgroup is still absent from a gene it is because it had no sequence for that locus.
- The **validation against Chazot et al. (2021)** and the project's own prior Danaini tree were
  done in separate notebooks; they are not part of this multi-locus build.
- Step 1 (`1_pull_ncbi_data.Rmd`) is the separate retrieval notebook that populates `input_data/`.
